newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Tractebel outperforms on mixed Belgian bourse.
newsitem.headline: Tractebel outperforms on mixed Belgian bourse.

text.p: Belgian shares ended mixed on Tuesday, but strength in Tractebel and holdings SGB and GBL helped the Bel-20 index outperform neighbouring markets.
"If the Dow can recoup some of its losses - as it is beginning to do -- we could see the market being rather positive (overall) tomorrow," one dealer said.
Wall Street returned from Monday's holiday in a negative mood, though by the time the Belgian bourse had closed the Dow was 15 points down at 5,600, above the day's low of 5,561.46.
The Bel-20 ended 2.31 points or 0.13 percent down at 1,717.16, with 1.9 billion francs of Belgian shares traded.

Leading Bel-20 component in terms of gains and volume was utility Tractebel, which ended 500 francs up at 13,425 after peaking at 13,550. SGB rose 15 francs to 2,400 and fellow holding GBL climbed 25 to 3,840.

The stocks were boosted by an unconfirmed article in Belgian newspaper the Financieel Economische Tijd which said GBL and affiliated companies were willing to sell their stake in Tractebel to SGB for 14,500 francs a share.
Electrafina, part of the GBL group, finished 110 francs up at 2,820. The company said in the afternoon it had considered selling its Tractebel stake but there had been no decision.
BBL, which reports first half earnings on Wednesday, held up better than other banks and closed unchanged at 5,870.

"As with the entire Belgian financial sector we expect BBL to release very good half year results...benefiting from a higher net interest margin - we expect at least a 17 percent jump to above 27 billion francs," Generale Bank said in a research note.
